hook: When you jump from writing an email to checking a quick Slack message, your brain doesn't actually switch instantly.
body: When you switch tasks, a portion of your attention stays glued to the previous activity. Researchers call this attention residue. It means that while you are trying to draft a proposal, your brain is still actively processing the chat message you just closed. This mental friction typically makes simple tasks take much longer and leaves you feeling completely drained by five o'clock, even if you did not finish anything substantial. Instead of doing deep work, your brain is stuck in a loop of constantly rebuilding context for each new task. That is why a highly fragmented day can feel incredibly exhausting while producing very little actual progress.
cta: Block out just ninety minutes tomorrow morning for one single, uninterrupted project.
